payload.title: Bag-out stops or remains in request while AGV or exchange-pair sequence appears abnormal
payload.user_facing_summary: Use this troubleshooting path when the site reports bag-out stopped after sorting, bag-out remains in request or does not complete, or operators suspect a robot, AGV pair, or exchange-pair sequencing problem. The response pattern is to confirm the bag-out symptom, inspect AGV and pair state in RMS, check whether a stuck task or hospital/HMI-only fault is involved, perform approved AGV pair or AGV sequence recovery if authorized, and validate that robots are back in proper sequence and bag-out can proceed.
payload.playbook_goal: Restore normal bag-out and robot operation by identifying and correcting AGV, exchange-pair, or stuck-task-related abnormal state without assuming a confirmed root cause.
observed_entry_symptoms: System stopped at bag-out after sorting
Bag-out entered request state and did not complete normally
Site manually bagged out while the issue was active
Operators suspected one of the exchange pairs or a robot out of sequence
An AGV was reported as not moving for an extended period
A fault relevant to the issue may only be visible on the hospital HMI or related HMI screen
payload.confidence_reason: The incident provides a coherent troubleshooting shape around bag-out stoppage, AGV/pair sequencing checks, HMI-visible stuck-task context, and recovery by restoring robot sequence. Confidence is reduced because the evidence is fragmented, some OCR is garbled, and the exact diagnostic boundaries between pair issue, stuck task, hospital HMI fault, and specific AGV removal are not fully explicit.

linked_runbooks.title: Recover an AGV That Lost a Tote Without an AGV Fault
linked_runbooks.summary: Restore the AGV and the missing tote to the system after an AGV loses a tote without the AGV itself faulting. The source sequence stops RMS, manually releases and moves the AGV to the Hospital, removes and re-adds the AGV at the Hospital station PC, power-cycles the AGV, repositions it at the Inbound Hospital Station QR code after its lights turn green, then removes and re-adds the missing tote.
linked_runbooks.when_to_use: Use when the AGV LOST TOTE NO FAULT recovery scenario applies and the AGV has lost a tote without the AGV itself faulting, using the recovery sequence documented in section 5.8.2.6.
not_for: Do not use for AGV fault scenarios not identified as "AGV LOST TOTE NO FAULT".
Do not use if the referenced Add/Remove AGV, Remove Tote, or Add Tote procedures cannot be completed.

responsibilities: E-stop RMS.

Locate the missing tote, bring it to the Hospital, remove it from the system, and add it back into the system using the referenced procedures.

The recovery includes E-stop use, brake release, manual AGV movement, and AGV/tote removal and re-addition actions.
Only maintenance or a supervisor should remove an AGV from the system, per the Add/Remove AGV screen reference.

payload.user_facing_summary: Use this response path when the site reports that the hospital area cannot add or induct totes, robots may appear shut down or misplaced, or sort cannot start because hospital flow is blocked. The path first confirms the observable hospital-flow symptom, then checks for AGV location or tote-association anomalies in the hospital area, then checks whether hospital-related services show an abnormal server/service condition, then performs the approved recovery path and validates that tote handling and robot flow resume.

linked_runbooks.title: Recover an AGV That Lost a Tote Without Faulting
linked_runbooks.summary: Restore an AGV and tote to service after an AGV loses a tote without faulting by stopping RMS, manually moving the AGV to the Hospital, removing and re-adding the AGV at the Hospital station PC, power cycling the AGV, positioning it over the QR code in front of the Inbound Hospital Station, and removing and re-adding the missing tote so the AGV can return the tote to the sorter.
linked_runbooks.when_to_use: Use when an AGV has lost a tote without faulting and must be restored to service through the Hospital workflow described in section 5.8.2.6.
not_for: Do not use when the AGV is faulted; the packet references separate faulted-AGV recovery content.
Do not use when the missing tote cannot be removed or added back using the documented tote procedures.
Do not use when the AGV cannot be physically moved to the Hospital or cannot be re-added through the Hospital station PC.

responsibilities: E-stop RMS.
Use the AGV brake release and manually move the AGV to the Hospital.
Remove and re-add the AGV at the Hospital station PC/Hospital HMI.
Power cycle the AGV and verify the AGV lights turn green.
Position the AGV over the QR code in front of the Inbound Hospital Station.
Locate the missing tote and complete tote removal and add-back using the documented procedures.

safety_notes: This procedure is not marked support-safe in the candidate.
The procedure includes E-stop use, brake release use, manual AGV movement, and AGV power cycling.
Only maintenance or a supervisor should remove an AGV from the system, per the Add/Remove AGV source reference attached to the Hospital HMI screen artifact.

payload.title: Site-wide robotic motion stoppage with AGVs out of sync after control-service or gateway abnormality
payload.user_facing_summary: Use this response pattern when a site reports that nothing is moving, the robotic system is not responding, small sort is stopped, or hospital/tote handling is blocked, and support needs to determine whether a control service or gateway issue is present, recover the affected service path if authorized, correct any AGVs left out of sync in RMS, and validate that automated operation has resumed.
payload.playbook_goal: Restore robotic system responsiveness and synchronized AGV operation after a site-wide stoppage by confirming service or gateway abnormality, performing approved recovery, correcting residual AGV sync issues in RMS, and validating stable recovery.
observed_entry_symptoms: Site reports that nothing is moving.
Robotic system is reported as not responding.
Small sort is not running.
Totes cannot be removed from hospital.
HMI or RMS appears abnormal, including question marks or a mostly blank page.
AGVs are reported out of sync or behaving abnormally after the stoppage.
affected_systems_or_components: Windows Event Viewer / Service Control Manager
payload.confidence_reason: The incident packet contains a clear troubleshooting path: confirm site-wide stoppage and abnormal UI state, inspect Event Viewer and service state, perform gateway or service recovery if authorized, use RMS to locate and correct out-of-sync AGVs, then validate via Ignition status, Windows Services, API response, and site recovery comments.

payload.title: Zone unable to get a pair with AMRs diverting to hospital after recent robot handling
payload.user_facing_summary: Use this response pattern when a site reports that an affected zone cannot get a pair and replacement or multiple AMRs are going to the hospital lane after recent low-battery, remove/add, or replacement activity. The incident evidence supports checking RMS for abnormal roster or mapping state, using approved AGV removal/isolation procedures when a specific robot appears abnormal or unmapped, and validating that pairing and AMR behavior return to normal after the action.
payload.playbook_goal: Restore normal pairing and AMR flow by identifying whether recent AGV handling left an abnormal roster or mapping condition in RMS and, if supported, isolating the affected robot and validating recovery.
observed_entry_symptoms: Affected zone reported as unable to get a pair
ACB system reported down or production seriously impacted
Replacement or multiple AMRs reported as going to the hospital lane
Issue reported after low-battery AMR trouble, robot replacement, or remove/add activity
payload.confidence_reason: The incident shows a coherent troubleshooting shape: observable pairing failure and hospital diversion, support suspicion of remove/add or roster issues, site removal of a specific robot reported as not mapped, and short-term recovery monitoring. Confidence is reduced because RMS screenshot details are partly unreadable, the exact decision criteria are not fully documented, and recovery is reported narratively rather than independently validated by clear live UI evidence.
